Hard constraint: every pair on a policy's ladder, including the tuned pick, has a paired 95% CI on the across-seed objective difference that excludes zero AND orders identically on 9/9 seeds. Among the triples meeting that, the one maximising the tightest rung was taken. '_mean=X' is the across-seed mean of macro_by_user_group_mean.ndcg@10, matching the ml-1m convention.

Ladder rungs in tuning ndcg@10, each the drop from the level above, top down — ALSPolicy: 0.0205/0.0200/0.0209; BPRPolicy: 0.0562/0.0501/0.0316; ItemKNNPolicy: 0.0238/0.0046/0.0099; LightGCNTorchPolicy: 0.0195/0.0419/0.0068.

CAVEAT: separability above is measured on the tuning validation split (57333 users, ndcg@10). The experiment scores mean_hit_rate on 1000 eval users, where a paired bootstrap on the ml-1m 15-policy run resolves adjacent rungs only from about 0.010 upward. ItemKNNPolicy (2 rungs at 0.0099 and 0.0046) and LightGCNTorchPolicy (1 rung at 0.0068) are expected to produce near-ties in the run; their grids have no wider-spaced alternative. ALSPolicy and BPRPolicy clear the bar on every rung.
